A SILVER Alert is an alert issued by emergency management agencies in the United States that informs the public of a missing and/or endangered senior citizen, who is disabled or has a medical condition (usually Dementia or Alzheimer's), or children and adults with mental disabilities. It is similar to an AMBER Alert, although it is not as widely publicized. SILVER Alerts do not have their own standalone SAME code and are usually issued as a Civil Emergency Message (CEM), an Administrative Message (ADR) or Law Enforcement Warning (LEW) . Contents 1 Who issues it? 2 Why is it issued? 3 Where can I see it? 4 What Should I Do? 5 Image Who issues it?[] SILVER Alerts are issued by Local Authorities and emergency management agencies. Why is it issued?[] SILVER Alerts are issued if a senior citizen is missing and/or in danger. Although slightly varying in some areas, several criteria have to be met for a SILVER Alert to be activated: The missing person is 65 years of age or older, developmentally disabled or cognitively impaired. The investigating law enforcement agency has utilized all available local resources. The law enforcement agency determines that the person has gone missing under unexplained or suspicious circumstances. The law enforcement agency believes that the person is in danger because of age, health, mental or physical disability, environment or weather conditions. The person is in the company of a potentially dangerous person, or other factors indicating that the person may be in peril. There is information available that, if disseminated to the public, could assist in the safe recovery of the missing person. Some states expand silver alerts to include children and adults with medical conditions. Where can I see it?[] SILVER Alerts are usually sent through the Wireless Emergency Alert System in most areas that relay them, however, select locations broadcast them over TV, radio and NOAA Weather Radio. What Should I Do?[] If you know anything about the last known whereabouts, or if you see the elder, please call 911, they will be taken care of.
